Posterior draws of residuals from mvgam models

Source: R/residuals.mvgam.R
residuals.mvgam.Rd

Posterior draws of the residuals of a fitted mvgam model, of two types:

  • "quantile" (default): randomised quantile residuals (Dunn and Smyth 1996), also called Dunn-Smyth or PIT residuals. Each observation passes through the distribution function of its predictive distribution, then through the standard normal quantile function. Under a correctly specified model the residuals are independent N(0, 1) draws for any response family.

  • "ordinary": the predictive error, y minus a posterior_predict.mvgam() draw, per draw.

In sample, both types compare each observation with predictions that condition on the latent trend state the model inferred at that time, the state hindcast.mvgam() returns. For newdata the fit has no such state. The predictions then use the covariate part of the model, without the trend's innovations. Passing process_error = TRUE adds them. pp_check.mvgam() and predictive_error.mvgam() use the same predictions.

Pearson residuals are not supported. A Pearson residual of a count or a bounded response is skewed and discrete even under a correctly specified model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
residuals(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("quantile", "ordinary"),
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object.

newdata

Optional data.frame to compute residuals on. Defaults to the training data.

type

Character. Either "quantile" (default) or "ordinary".

ndraws

Positive integer specifying number of posterior draws to use. NULL (default) uses all available draws.

draw_ids

Optional integer vector selecting a subset of posterior draw indices to use. NULL (default) uses all draws (subject to ndraws).

summary

Logical. TRUE (the default) returns a summary per observation. FALSE returns the residual draws.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

probs

Two probabilities for the lower and upper quantile columns of the summary. Default c(0.025, 0.975), a 95% interval.

...

Further arguments of posterior_predict.mvgam(), such as resp or re_formula.

Value

With summary = FALSE, an [ndraws, nobs] matrix of residual draws. A continuous family on the empirical route has one interval per observation. Its rows are then identical. With summary = TRUE, an [nobs, 2 + length(probs)] matrix. Its columns are Estimate (the mean, or the median with robust = TRUE), Est.Error (the standard deviation, or the MAD) and one quantile per probs.

Details

Each draw places an observation in a PIT interval [lower, upper]. The residual is qnorm(u) for a u drawn uniformly from that interval. Two routes give the interval.

The analytic route evaluates the family's distribution function at each draw's parameters. A discrete family gives the interval of the observed atom, [F(y - 1), F(y)]. A continuous family gives the point F(y). A tweedie() zero gives [0, F(0)]. Censored rows span their censoring interval. A truncated model renormalises over its truncation bounds. log_lik.mvgam() takes its density from the same parameterisation. The route covers gaussian, student, asym_laplace, lognormal, gamma, weibull, exponential, beta, bernoulli, binomial, beta_binomial, poisson, negbinomial, geometric, com_binomial(), beta_nb(), tweedie(), the ordinal families, and the multivariate mvn(), mvt(), diri(), multi() and categ(). A composition family uses the marginal of one component: a Beta for diri(), a Binomial against the site's own total for multi() and a Bernoulli for categ().

Every other family takes the empirical route of DHARMa (Hartig 2024), among them the zero-inflated, hurdle and mixture families, occ() and nmix(). The bounds are mean(yrep < y) and mean(yrep <= y) over the pooled posterior_predict.mvgam() draws. The pooled predictive carries the posterior uncertainty in the latent state. Its residuals are narrower than N(0, 1). A QQ-plot of them is conservative.

The PIT value is clamped to [eps, 1 - eps], with eps = .Machine$double.eps, to keep the residual finite. The clamp bounds a residual at about +/-8.13. On the analytic route one draw can place an observation beyond that bound. Such isolated values describe that draw. A misfit shifts the residual across most draws. The empirical route reaches the clamp whenever an observation lies outside every simulated value. With few draws that happens often. Use ndraws >= 500 there, the default of the residual histograms and ribbons of pp_check.mvgam().

Multivariate families (mvn(), mvt(), diri())

Each row of a unit gets its own residual. Residuals of mvn() and mvt() condition on the latent factor scores and test the observation model. They stay N(0, 1) when the fit has too few factors. active_factors() and residual_cor.mvgam() judge the number of factors.

A diri() residual is the exact marginal of one component, Beta(alpha_j, alpha_0 - alpha_j). Each is N(0, 1) on its own. Because the shares of a unit sum to one, the residuals of a unit of K species are negatively dependent, with K - 1 degrees of freedom. With K = 2 the two residuals are exactly antithetic. Judge a QQ-plot or an ACF at the unit grain.

Closure-unit families (nmix(), occ())

Visits within a closure unit (site by season) share the latent state, N for nmix() and z for occ(). The visits are independent given that state, but dependent marginally. Because residuals per visit would carry that dependence into every diagnostic, residuals() returns one residual per closure unit. The observed counts or detections are summed within each unit. The visit-level posterior_predict.mvgam() draws are summed the same way. Columns (summary = FALSE) or rows (summary = TRUE) are labelled by the unit's grouping values joined with _.

Each draw simulates the latent state from lambda or psi without conditioning on the unit's detection history. The residuals then test the model across the population of units. predict(type = "latent_state") gives the state given each unit's detection history.

Under occ() a unit sum takes values in 0, ..., n_rep. With few visits the empirical PIT has coarse support. QQ-plot tails then look heavier than N(0, 1) under a correctly specified model. A once-per-session warning is raised when any unit has 4 or fewer visits. Compare QQ-plots with envelopes simulated from N(0, 1) in that case.

References

Dunn, P. K. and Smyth, G. K. (1996). Randomized quantile residuals. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 5(3), 236-244.

Hartig, F. (2024). DHARMa: Residual diagnostics for hierarchical (multi-level / mixed) regression models. R package. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=DHARMa

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
             data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
             chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Quantile residuals summarised per observation
r <- residuals(mod)
head(r)
#>         Estimate Est.Error       Q2.5      Q97.5
#> [1,]  0.04305444 0.6276094 -1.2293330  1.2065680
#> [2,]  0.43102182 0.9100175 -1.4328467  2.1089368
#> [3,]  0.08381852 0.7538234 -1.3775664  1.5728609
#> [4,] -1.66884248 0.6492969 -2.9454988 -0.3349742
#> [5,]  0.74917410 0.7539337 -0.7791357  2.2124208
#> [6,]  0.11081097 0.7590387 -1.4080932  1.5538332

# One draw of the residuals should look like N(0, 1) draws
r1 <- residuals(mod, summary = FALSE, draw_ids = 1)
qqnorm(r1[1, ])
qqline(r1[1, ])


# Next: plot(mod, type = "residuals") draws the QQ-plot, ACF and
# residuals against fitted values over many draws. A series observed
# at unevenly spaced times gets a semivariogram in place of the ACF
# }
